To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) RX J1605 is a young NS, (2) it is probably a runaway star, (3) it was born in a SN event, (4) the SN occurred in the Octans or the Corona Australis associations, and (5) it was a progenitor with a mass of about 11M⊕.
RX J1605 is likely a member of the Octans association and was born in a SN that occurred ≈ 0.45Myr ago, ≈100pc away from Earth.

RX J1605 is most likely an isolated NS that was probably born 0.45-3.5 Myrs ago ≈100 pc away from Earth in the extended Corona Austrina/Octans associations or in Sco OB 4, and that the SN that created this NS was accompanied by a feature in the 26Al γ-ray emission that is consistent with a 26Al production of 2.5 × 10^45 26Al nuclei.
